text:
jordan: quick sanity check — after the kernel selection tweak on the 8-bit path, we started seeing a spike in soft 429s on the p99. seen this in canary and a couple prod clusters. anyone else?
lee: yes. reproduced locally. batch formation collapsed to many microbatches (mostly size 1/2) for sequences ~120 tokens. CPU on host jumped, kernels fell back to slower path.
anya: profiler snapshot from canary attached in thread (summary below). p50 latency +8ms, p95 +30ms, p99 +120ms vs baseline. KV hit-rate unchanged.
sam: can you paste the profiling highlights? want to check if it's KV eviction thrash or kernel mismatch.
lee: pasted sample: 
```
wall_time_ms: 210
kernel: aten_small_seq_opt (fallback)
batch_size: 1..3 (median 2)
kv_cache_reads: 0.98
token_budget_used: 140
queue_wait_ms: 18
```
lee: key point: batcher encoded a very short assemble window due to the token_governor hitting a conservative target. That reduced batching headroom and pushed kernels onto the non-optimized path.
miguel: interesting — last week's tuning lowered token_budget target to 120 for better tail in large batches, but maybe it's too low for mixed seq lengths.
jordan: hypothesis: token governor window too tight + prefetch disabled -> microbatches + kernel swap. Need to test increasing token target or relaxing window_ms.
anya: quick experiment suggestion: two toggles — raise token_target to 200 and increase assemble_window_ms from 8 to 16 on one canary pool. Compare kernel selection histogram + microbatch sizes.
sam: also add a KV-prefetch probe: enable prefix prefetch for sequences >64 to warm KV and reduce queue_wait jitter.
lee: config snippet I'll run on canary: 
```yaml
batcher:
  assemble_window_ms: 16
  token_governor:
    target_tokens: 200
    window_ms: 100
prefetch:
  enabled: true
  min_seq: 64
```
lee: running now on canary-3 (slot 5). starting traffic ramp 100rps -> 200rps over 10m.
miguel: run with perf counters: kernel_choice, batch_size_hist, kv_hit_per_req. set debug log sample rate 1%.
jordan: good. what are our success criteria? p99 back to baseline, reduced fallbacks to aten_small_seq_opt <1% of requests, batch median >= 6 for seq>64.
anya: and watch for cost: raising token target may increase latency for small seqs if we wait too long. watch p50 and error budget.
sam: note: if we see queue wait > 40ms we should ramp token_target down again. set an automated rollback.
lee: canary deployed config at +2m. initial observations after 5m: median batch size for seq>64 jumped from 2 -> 7. kernel_choice: optimized_path increased from 68% -> 94%. p99 latency falling ~90ms. kv-prefetch hit-rate up slightly.
jordan: awesome. any regressions?
lee: a small p50 increase (2ms) for seq<32, likely waiting longer to form batch. within budget for now.
miguel: cost check: token burn approx +3% for canary traffic, but throughput improved. seems fine.
anya: let's keep the canary running for 2 hours and collect kernel histograms + tracing. If stable, roll to additional pools.
sam: add soft limit tweak: change soft_reject_threshold from 0.92 -> 0.95 so we tolerate slightly higher utilization before shedding. reduces false-429s while governor warms.
jordan: deploy-bot can we gate the broader rollout on the canary metrics? create a rollout plan with automated checks.
deploy-bot: rollout created: prefetch-token-governor-2415 -> canary-3. gates: p99_latency_delta <= +10ms, optimized_path_rate >= 90%, soft_429_rate <= 0.5% over 10m windows. Auto-rollback on fail. :rocket:
lee: logging note: add a short probe that records kernel switch reasons. helps correlate when sequence length distribution triggers fallback.
miguel: we should also capture kv cache pressure spikes. maybe increase kv_capacity by 5% on canary to observe sensitivity.
anya: agreed. set kv_capacity_delta +5%. monitor eviction_rate.
lee: after 30m: canary stable. p99 within +5ms baseline, optimized_path 92%, batch median 6. rollout ready.
jordan: plan: 2-stage rollout to 4 more pools over 2 hours, with the same gates. sam will own canary->stage rollout.
sam: will kick off at +45m. I'll post results if any anomalies.
anya: follow-up todo: run a synthetic with skewed small-seq load to verify no regressions.
miguel: add to postmortem template: "kernel-governor interaction" checklist.
jordan: thanks team. great catch and quick iteration. :tada:
deploy-bot: stage rollout started -> pool-7. monitoring gates...
